Run SQL on the server

spark_sql.Rd

spark_sql() sends a statement to the server. A command (DDL, DML, SET, SHOW, a SQL script) runs at once, and its rows come back as a data frame. A query (SELECT, WITH, VALUES, ...) comes back as a zuspark_query, which holds the server's plan for it and no rows; it runs when spark_collect() or spark_fetch() asks for them, and runs again on every such call. spark_execute() runs a statement for its effect and discards its rows.

Usage

spark_sql(con, sql)

spark_execute(con, sql)

Arguments

con

A zuspark_connection.

sql

A Spark SQL statement, as a single string.

Value

spark_sql() returns a zuspark_query for a query, or a data frame for a command. spark_execute() returns the number of rows the statement produced, invisibly.

Examples

con <- spark_connect()
q <- spark_sql(con, "SELECT id, id * 2 AS twice FROM range(5)")
q
#> <zuspark_query> SELECT id, id * 2 AS twice FROM range(5)
#>   on sc://127.0.0.1:15002 (not run yet)
spark_collect(q)
#>   id twice
#> 1  0     0
#> 2  1     2
#> 3  2     4
#> 4  3     6
#> 5  4     8
spark_sql(con, "SHOW DATABASES")
#>   namespace
#> 1   default
spark_disconnect(con)
